composers_checked.name: Boccherini, Luigi
composers_checked.note: Gap check against Gérard's catalogue (musiqueorguequebec.ca/catal/boccherini, Wikipedia list). Added, not on IMSLP: Op. 64 Nos. 1–2 (G. 248–249), flute quintets G. 437–442, notturni G. 470 and G. 472; also the 1781 Stabat Mater from an out-of-scope IMSLP page. Not added for want of a recording: quartets Op. 9 Nos. 1, 3–5, Op. 24 Nos. 2–5, Op. 42 (G. 216–217), Op. 43 (G. 218–219), Op. 44 Nos. 1–3, 5–6, Op. 48 (G. 226–231), Op. 53 Nos. 2–6; sextet G. 471.

note: c28 Boccherini, string quartets and mixed ensembles: one composer, covered completely. Scoring and dates from IMSLP (api.php wikitext) and Gérard's thematic catalogue as published at musiqueorguequebec.ca; floor and durations (means of the Apple Music track timings) from Apple Music (iTunes Search API) and MusicBrainz. Titles use Boccherini's own opus numbers (Gérard); the Paris publication numbers are in aka. Judgment calls: (1) Op. 2 and Op. 33 rest on CPO albums whose ensemble Apple Music does not name (CPO's 6-CD set of 24 quartets gives the Sonare Quartett, Nomos Quartett and The Revolutionary Drawing Room); (2) Op. 22 rests on one 2026 recording (Concerto 1700, 1700 Classics); Op. 15 on one (Alea Ensemble, Dynamic); (3) the Sextet G. 467 rests on one self-released recording (Sally Walker, 2024), confidence medium; (4) the flute quintets G. 437–442 are added with the scoring given in the Rampal recording (flute, violin, viola, two cellos, as Wikipedia's 'with cello concertante'), although the online Gérard catalogue headings say 2 violins, viola and cello: check the scoring; (5) the Octet G. 470 is recorded by Tafelmusik (Sony Vivarte, 1993) and by the Stuttgart Chamber Orchestra (Goritzki): presumably one to a part as an octet, not verified; (6) the keyboard trios G. 143–148 are kept with harpsichord, as the first edition prints it ('pour le Clavecin'), formation 'other'; the only recording (Galimathias Musicum) uses fortepiano, so the owner may prefer piano (formation piano-trio); (7) the Stabat Mater G. 532 was filed by the census as string orchestra; its 1781 first version is for soprano and string quintet one to a part (IMSLP) and is recorded so (L'Archibudelli; Ensemble 415), so it is kept as a vocal chamber work (orchestrator's request); the 1800 version for three voices and strings is not listed. Not listed: G. 443–444 (flute, oboe and strings; 'incorrectly attributed to Boccherini' in Gérard, though G. 443 is recorded under his name), the wind quartets G. 262–264 (arrangements by O. Van den Broeck, no strings), the keyboard quartets G. 259 (arrangements of Op. 26 by an unknown hand), the quartets G. 250–257 (arrangements and doubtful works), the flute quartets G. 260–261 (arrangements, partly lost), the trios for flutes and continuo G. 157–158 (arrangements), and the lost works G. 452, 468, 469, 473. Boccherini's piano quintets, string trios, string quintets and sextets belong to the c27 and c29 slices. Orchestrator (by hand): G. 143–148 entered with piano and harpsichord as the alternative and titled "Piano Trio", as the brief treats Classical-era keyboards and as c24 did for Haydn's 'cembalo' trios.
